The test I wrote aims to verify the width of the Nerd Font character `\U000f024d`.
I'm using `Console(width=80, _environ={})` to ensure a consistent environment for measurement, as `rich` can be sensitive to terminal capabilities.
The `console.measure(text)` method returns a `Measurement` object, from which I extract `maximum` width.
The expectation is that this character, being a single Unicode character, should have a width of 1. If the bug exists, it will report 2.

Let's run this test and see the outcome.", "tool": "run_test", "args": {"source": "import pytest
from rich.console import Console
from rich.text import Text

def test_nerd_font_width():
    console = Console(width=80, _environ={})
    # The problematic Nerd Font character (f024d is a download folder icon)
    nerd_font_char = "\U000f024d"
    text = Text(nerd_font_char)

    # Measure the width of the text
    measurement = console.measure(text)

    # The character should be single-width
    expected_width = 1
    actual_width = measurement.maximum

    assert actual_width == expected_width, f"Expected width {expected_width}, but got {actual_width} for character {nerd_font_char}"
"}}
